verdicts.flaw_description: "The counts cover the sessions that reached the new page, and a quarter of each segment dropped out before checkout." The outcome is measured only on a filtered subset of each segment while a quarter of the segment is dropped from the count, so the measured group is self-selected rather than the whole segment; a shift in who survives to checkout, not the new page, could produce the 4-7 percent gap against the earlier month.

"A higher-yielding seed line replaced the previous one across the estate that season, and every block was sown from the estate's general seed stock." A yield-raising change other than the drip line hit every measured block in the same season, so the 0.4-0.7 t/ha gain over the previous summer is fully confounded with the seed change; the report even confirms all blocks were exposed to it.

The measurement dates precede the start dates in three of the four groups: "started 4 March, measured by 28 February", "started 5 September, measured by 30 August", and "started 26 November, measured by 2 October". The reduction in attacks was recorded before the inhaler was started, so those observations cannot be effects of the inhaler (the season labels, e.g. "winter quarter, started 4 March", are also inconsistent).

"Averages cover the patients who kept up the home exercises, and a quarter of each intake let the home exercises lapse." The abduction averages are computed only on the compliant survivors while a quarter of each intake is excluded, and they are compared against a prior-quarter ward figure that was not filtered the same way; selecting the most adherent patients can produce the 9-16 degree gain on its own.

"Class sizes at each school ran about a quarter below the year before, and every logged class took its English lessons as one whole group." Class size dropped roughly 25 percent across all logged classes in the same period as the program, and the report confirms every class was taught in that reduced whole-group setting, so the 5-9 point comprehension gain over the previous autumn cannot be separated from the smaller classes.

"Rates cover the boards soldered on the new profile throughout, and about a tenth of each run's boards took one pass on the old profile." The defect rate is computed only on the purely new-profile boards, dropping about a tenth of each run - exactly the mixed/reworked boards most likely to carry defects - while the earlier-month baseline included all boards, so the 4-7 percent drop can come from the exclusion rather than the profile.
